_comment: The NESTED submission layout, and the only fixture that has one: --sca-root is the archive, the add-on code sits in addon/ and the Experiment implementation under addon/experiment/. Every other SCA fixture is FLAT (--sca-source IS --sca-root), where an empty prefix keys a file identically in the archive and in the review source - so a flat fixture cannot tell the two keyspaces apart, and cannot reach any path arithmetic that runs against a non-empty source prefix. This one holds both keyspaces side by side, so a drift between them shows up as a golden diff. What it pins: the source's own manifest is read from addon/, so its __MSG_extName__ name resolves against addon/_locales and no localization finding fires; main.js is reviewed, which its fake namespace reports; the VENDOR file is found at the ROOT OF THE SOURCE and its declaration `lib/widget.js` resolves relative to the ADD-ON, not the archive - offline nothing verifies, so applyUnverifiedVendor reconciles it into the untrusted family and unsafe-html reads the file as authored code; the --sca-exp-source exclusion keeps core-symbol-in-webext silent on the privileged ChromeUtils call (drop the flag and it reports experiment/exp.js, which is what makes the exclusion load-bearing here rather than incidental) - while unsafe-html still reports the innerHTML sink in that same file, because the exclusion is scoped to the WebExtension API/permission checks and a file is still reviewed for WHAT IT IS (privileged code shipped with a sink, minified or obfuscated is worse, not exempt); build.js sits outside the source, so it is build tooling and its own fake namespace is never reported. package.json and its lock are at the archive root where they belong, so the build checks stay silent and the build-review escalation anchors there - the one archive-relative path in the report.
